label: Building type
description: Building types and recognizable structures: homes, places of worship, civic buildings, industry, and transport.
notes: Buildings and freestanding built structures belong here, named as singular types after “a.” A few vowel-initial names carry a short identifying modifier so the frame reads naturally. Architectural treatments belong in place.architecture_style, and decorated room settings belong in interior_space.style. Less familiar structures have visual glosses, as do common ones for consistent browsing; multifunctional buildings may appear in several kind groups.

values.look: A detached dwelling with its own entrance, windows, roof, and surrounding yard.
A narrow masonry townhouse with a brown stone facade and a raised front stoop.
A narrow house shares side walls with matching neighboring homes in a continuous street frontage.
A very narrow house has a front porch and rooms arranged one behind another.
A dense apartment building has repetitive windows, shared entrances, and exterior fire escapes.
An ornate Victorian wooden house is painted in several contrasting colors that highlight its trim.
Two steep roof slopes extend almost to the ground, forming a triangular house.
Stacked horizontal logs form a small dwelling with visible notched corners and a pitched roof.
A low house has a broad roof, a sheltered front porch, and most rooms on one floor.
A long narrow communal dwelling has a continuous roof over many bays and a series of entrances.
A round felt-covered dwelling has a low conical roof and a central roof opening.
A small rounded shelter is built from fitted snow blocks with a low tunnel entrance.
A small elevated dwelling rests among tree branches with a ladder or raised walkway.
A dwelling stands on tall posts above water or sloping ground, reached by steps.
A floating dwelling has cabin windows, deck railings, and a broad buoyant hull.
A compact dwelling has a small porch, closely packed windows, and often a trailer base.
A home uses corrugated steel cargo boxes with doors and windows cut into the sides.
A bermed home has a long sloping glass front, thick earth walls, and embedded bottle details.
A low grass-covered mound encloses a cozy house with a round front door and small round windows.
A house encloses a planted courtyard with a fountain, tiled surfaces, and inward-facing balconies.
A large urban residence has a heavy masonry street front, tall windows, and an inner courtyard.
A grand country residence has steep roofs, stone facades, formal grounds, and towers or turrets.
A massive fortified stone tower has thick walls, narrow openings, and a battlemented top.
Fortified walls and towers rise behind a surrounding water-filled moat and bridge.
Low thick defensive walls form pointed bastions in a star-shaped earthwork plan.
A tall narrow defensive tower has small windows and an elevated lookout platform.
A prayer hall has a broad entrance, often accompanied by domes, a courtyard, and minarets.
A tall slender tower has one or more small balconies and a pointed or domed cap.
A large church has a long nave, a monumental entrance, and prominent towers or a dome.
A dark timber church has steep layered roofs, vertical plank walls, and carved roof finials.
Bulb-shaped domes taper to crosses above colorful towers and arched church walls.
A tall tower has multiple stacked roofs with projecting, often upturned eaves.
A solid domed Buddhist monument sits on a raised base beneath a spire and small square railing.
A massive mud-brick temple platform rises in broad rectangular stepped terraces.
A monumental structure has sloping triangular faces that meet at a high point.
A sculpted sanctuary tower rises above a columned hall and carved stone walls.
A timber sanctuary has a steep roof, a raised veranda, and a freestanding torii gate nearby.
A Jewish worship building has a main sanctuary entrance, often marked with Hebrew lettering or a Star of David.
A religious compound encloses courtyards or cloisters surrounded by halls, cells, and a place of worship.
A rectangular stone sanctuary has a surrounding colonnade and a triangular pediment.
A prominent public building has a formal entrance, broad steps, and often a central clock tower.
A public reading building has generous windows, a welcoming entrance, and visible book-lined interiors.
A formal civic building has broad entrance steps, imposing doors, and often a columned front.
Wide vehicle bays line a public building with firefighting equipment or engines visible inside.
A small classroom building has tall regular windows, a simple entrance, and often a bell tower.
A public exhibition building has a broad entrance and large gallery volumes, often with banners outside.
A communal bathing building has a sheltered entrance, steam vents, and tiled or domed bathing halls.
A tall rectilinear office building has reflective glass curtain walls and a regular floor grid.
A very tall urban building rises far above its neighbors with many stacked floors.
A compact roadside restaurant has large windows, counter seating, and a long narrow footprint.
Fuel pumps stand under a broad canopy beside a small roadside shop.
A low roadside lodging block has repeated exterior room doors facing a parking lot.
A large outdoor movie screen faces rows of parking spaces and a small projection building.
A covered pedestrian passage is lined with shopfronts beneath glass or vaulted roofing.
A broad roof spans rows of vendor stalls with wide aisles and large public entrances.
A long semicylindrical corrugated-metal shell meets the ground on both sides.
A transparent glass or plastic shell covers rows of plants beneath a pitched or curved roof.
Large rotating sails rise above a tower or mill building, often with a cap that faces the wind.
An elevated tank sits on tall legs or a masonry shaft above the surrounding buildings.
A tall cylindrical grain store has smooth metal or concrete walls and a conical or domed top.
A large farm building has broad doors, a high roof, and open interior storage bays.
Large industrial sheds have repetitive window bays, loading doors, and chimneys or rooftop vents.
A broad storage building has few windows, large loading bays, and truck access.
A mill building stands beside moving water with a large paddle wheel fixed to one wall.
A huge hollow concrete tower narrows at the middle and releases a broad white plume.
An open fenced installation holds transformers, ceramic insulators, and steel electrical gantries.
A passenger building opens onto covered rail platforms with tracks and station signs.
A large glazed passenger hall connects to boarding bridges and aircraft on a broad apron.
A tall coastal tower has a glazed lantern room and balcony above a narrow stair-filled shaft.
A waterside building has wide doors or open bays that let boats enter directly from the water.
A huge clear-span shed has exceptionally wide sliding doors facing an airfield.
A small glazed booth stands between vehicle lanes under a protective canopy.
A semicircular engine shed has radiating tracks that meet at a central turntable.
A rounded rotating dome has a narrow open slit for a telescope above a supporting building.
Tiered seating forms a large bowl around a sports field, often ringed by floodlights.
A low public building is topped by a broad smooth hemispherical projection dome.
An open raised pavilion has a roof on slender posts and space for musicians.
A fortified roadside inn encloses a large courtyard behind a monumental arched gateway.
A small whitewashed stone dwelling has one or more pointed conical roofs of layered gray stone.
A roofed timber passage crosses water on a bridge deck, with side openings admitting light.
